summary: Iceland's only origin variable in crime data is a two-way split of suspects into Icelandic and foreign citizens on a police dashboard, for all victims. No child victims are published by citizenship or origin for any harm, and trafficking victims' nationality comes only from a US government report.

nations.National (Police, Barna- og fjölskyldust: Police suspects dashboard and sexual-offence reports; national child-protection figures.

european_title: Not recorded by any Icelandic source
european_note: Icelandic statistics record only citizenship (Icelandic or foreign), never ethnicity or parents' origin. Icelandic citizens include naturalised immigrants of any origin, and foreign citizens include Europeans and tourists, so ethnic Europeans cannot be identified.
proxy_note: Iceland records citizenship only, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Sexual offences (police suspects, all victims)
harms.intro: Police recorded 124 sexual offences against children in 2024 and 94 in January-September 2025, with no citizenship or origin of victims or suspects. The police suspects dashboard gives the share of Icelandic and foreign citizens among the 398 people suspected of sexual offences in 2025 (all victims, suspects aged 15 and over).

victims.text: Police and child-protection statistics on child victims publish no citizenship or origin.

perpetrators.scope: Iceland, suspects of sexual offences aged 15+, all victims, 2025
perpetrators.share_note: Icelandic Police dashboard 'Grunaðir einstaklingar skv. gögnum lögreglu 2019-2025': suspects aged 15 and over, read by selecting the offence category on 19 November 2026; percentages as shown on the dashboard. Over 2019-2025 as a whole, 76% of sexual-offence suspects were Icelandic citizens. Not child-specific. Citizenship, a proxy, not ethnicity: Icelandic citizens include naturalised immigrants, and foreign citizens include tourists and other non-residents (the police could not split the data by residence).

cross.text: No victim data by citizenship, so nothing can be linked.

harms.label: Child protection (Reykjavik team for children of foreign origin)
harms.intro: Child-protection services received 18,429 notifications in 2025, most for neglect, but national figures give no citizenship or origin. Reykjavik's child-protection report lists by country of origin only the 208 cases handled by its team for children of foreign origin (35% neglect, 27% physical violence, 25% witnessing domestic violence); by design almost all are of foreign origin, so these are not population figures.

victims.scope: Reykjavik, cases allocated to the investigation and treatment team for children of foreign origin, 2024
victims.share_note: Reykjavik child protection annual report 2024, Table 1: Poland 29, Romania 22, Iceland 20, Vietnam 16, Iraq 11, Ukraine 10, Somalia 8, Philippines 8, Afghanistan 7, Lithuania 7, 24 other countries 68. The team exists for children of foreign origin, so the split reflects case allocation, not risk. Country of origin, a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Homicide
harms.intro: No official statistics on homicide victims or perpetrators by citizenship or origin were found.

perpetrators.text: The dashboard has no homicide category.

harms.label: Trafficking in human beings
harms.intro: Iceland publishes no official trafficking statistics by nationality. The US State Department's 2025 report (a foreign-government source) says Icelandic authorities identified 37 trafficking victims in 2024 (10 sex trafficking, 20 labour, 7 unspecified), all foreign nationals; six were children. No trafficker data.

victims.scope: Iceland, trafficking victims identified by the authorities, all ages and forms, 2024
victims.share_note: Non-Icelandic source: US State Department, 2025 Trafficking in Persons Report. Nationality, a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Child sexual abuse material
harms.intro: Police recorded 40 offences involving child sexual abuse material in 2024 and 40 in January-September 2025, with no citizenship of victims or suspects; the dashboard has no separate category for them.

breakdown.why: The police dashboard of suspects 2019-2025 gives the Icelandic-citizen share of sexual-offence suspects aged 15+ (71% in 2025), all victims; the police report on sexual offences (124 against children in 2024, 94 in January-September 2025) gives no citizenship. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Reykjavík child protection publishes origin only for its team for children of foreign origin, which is not a population figure. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: Iceland scores 7% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. The only origin variable in Icelandic crime data is a two-way split of suspects into Icelandic and foreign citizens, with no child victims by origin for any harm; trafficking victims' nationality comes only from a US government report.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
